Article Title: Watch: PM Modi takes part in yoga session during Uzbekistan visit
Article Text:
Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan performed a Yoga session in presence of PM Modi

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi participated in a yoga session organised by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan in Tashkent on Sunday, during his two-day state visit to Uzbekistan.PM Modi walked around the venue and interacted with participants as the group performed yoga. He also posed for a group photograph with the participants at the end of the session.The yoga programme came a day after PM Modi received a warm welcome from Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev following his arrival in Tashkent. The two leaders travelled together from the airport to the presidential palace and later held a dinner meeting. "Landed in Tashkent to a warm welcome by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Grateful to him for the special gesture. This is my fourth visit to Uzbekistan, reflecting the depth and growing momentum of our bilateral relations," said the PM as he landed in Uzbekistan on Saturday.Later, the Prime Minister shared a video message hailing the session saying, "‘Uzbekistan loves yoga."In another social media post he further added, "Uzbekistan was a proud participant in the first ever World Yogasana Championship held in Ahmedabad earlier this year.Some of the medalists were also present today. They came back with great memories of India and the Championship. I commend the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan for their work towards making Yoga popular."The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Mirziyoyev later on Sunday, with discussions expected to focus on trade and investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy, education and people-to-people ties.The visit is PM Modi’s fourth to Uzbekistan since becoming prime minister, following trips in 2015, 2016 and 2022. He will travel to Bishkek next to attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit at the invitation of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov.
Article Summary: Yoga federation of uzbekistan performed a yoga session in presence of pm modi. Pm modi walked around the venue and interacted with participants as the group performed yoga. The yoga programme came a day after pm modi received a warm welcome from uzbek president shavkat mirziyoyev.

Article Title: PM Modi received by Uzbek President Mirziyoyev in Tashkent, leaders share car ride
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi with Uzbekistan Shavkat President Mirziyoyev

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PM Modi's 'car' diplomacy

Prime Minister Narendra Modi received a warm and personal welcome from Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev after arriving in capital Tashkent on Saturday for a two-day state visit.From the airport, the two leaders travelled together by car to the presidential palace, marking the latest instance of PM Modi sharing a car ride with a world leader. They held a dinner meeting at the presidential palace.During the visit, the first leg of the prime minister’s two-nation tour, PM Modi will hold delegation-level talks with the Uzbek president to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries.The discussions will cover cooperation in trade and investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy, education and people-to-people ties, while also setting the agenda for future bilateral engagement.In his departure statement, PM Modi noted that the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership had witnessed “significant advancement” in recent years.“I look forward to my discussions with President Mirziyoyev on further deepening our cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, energy, and on advancing our shared visions of Viksit Bharat and Yangi Uzbekistan,” he wrote on X.The visit marks his fourth trip to Uzbekistan since taking office.He previously visited the country in 2015, 2016 and 2022.From Tashkent, PM Modi will travel to Bishkek at the invitation of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov to attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit, which will mark 25 years of the organisation.PM Modi first “carpooled” with a world leader during his 2014 visit to the United States, when he shared a car ride with then-US President Barack Obama.However, since last year, car rides with world leaders have become a recurring feature of what has been described as the prime minister's "informal diplomacy."In September last year, during his visit to China for the SCO Summit, PM Modi travelled in the same car as Vladimir Putin, reciprocating the gesture months later when the Russian president visited New Delhi in December.Since then, he has shared car rides with world leaders including French President Emmanuel Macron, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi arrived in capital tashkent on saturday for a two-day state visit. He will hold delegation-level talks with the uzbek president to further strengthen the strategic partnership between the two countries. The visit marks his fourth trip to uzbekistan since taking office.

Article Title: 'If any Hindu thinks there should be no Muslims in India, he's not Hindu': RSS' Mohan Bhagwat in US
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday said Hinduism believes in the unity of humanity, asserting that “If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslims in India, then he's not a Hindu.”Addressing the ‘One World One Humanity’ event in New York, Bhagwat said different religions may follow different paths, but humanity and truth remain one.“We come from a society that believes humanity is one. If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslims in India, then he's not a Hindu….” the RSS chief said.“If you want call yourself hindu than you must believe that all paths are leading to the same. And every human has a dignity. There is no difference between human beings,” he added.Bhagwat said diversity must be protected while stressing the importance of unity. “Diversity has to be protected as it is the rule of nature and 'Unity is universal truth,” he said.“I am not a religious scholar, nor a religious authority like you, but I am working in a society which traditionally says that religions might be different, but humanity is one. Truth is one, and humanity is a product of that truth. So humanity is one,” Bhagwat said.He added that while truth is one, it can be described in different ways depending on how people perceive it.“That truth is one truth, but it is described in many ways according to the describer. Because as human beings, we are prisoners of the software that has been created in our heads,” he said.“There are many religions, and in today's world, religions are largely defined by rituals. And to fit in a religious discipline, and to treat that path to divinity, this discipline of rituals is also necessary,” he added.The RSS chief framed his address around the idea of “oneness”, drawing parallels between the pluralism associated with the United States and what he described as Bharat’s “unity in diversity”.“When we say America, United States of America, one word is often discussed frequently. That is pluralism,” Bhagwat said. “And when we say Bharat, another word, another phrase is discussed: unity in diversity.”“For Bharat, this unity and diversity, both are in their DNA,” he said.Read more: 'RSS vision is to see the world as one' - Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat at New York event The event was organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD) and was described as a “landmark Raksha Bandhan gathering”.“The event carries a timeless and universal message: 'The world is one family'. It calls upon us to look beyond artificial divisions and differences, recognise the bonds that unite humanity, and embrace a spirit of mutual respect, harmony, and oneness,” the organisation said.The programme featured cultural presentations and keynote addresses centred on universal oneness and the Hindu philosophy of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’, or the world is one family.Bhagwat arrived in the US earlier this week as part of the RSS's centenary-year global outreach programme, which also includes visits to Canada and the UK.During his visit, he has met members of the Indian diaspora, Indian-American business leaders and community representatives.Ahead of his Madison Square Garden address, images of Bhagwat were projected on billboards in New York's Times Square, carrying the words “Resolve, Harmony and Dialogue”.Bhagwat also visited the Bhakti Centre and the ISKCON temple in New York. At the temple, he participated in a food distribution initiative for homeless people and spoke about the role of Krishna consciousness in addressing conflicts and divisions.Before, the RSS had said that the Madison Square Garden event was being organised in the spirit of open dialogue and invited “anyone interested” in learning more about the organisation to participate.
Article Summary: Rss chief mohan bhagwat said hinduism believes in the unity of humanity. He said different religions may follow different paths, but humanity and truth remain one. “if any hindu thinks that there should be no muslims in india, then he's not a hindu,” he said.

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he's looking forward to advancing India's vision for the region anchored in security, connectivity and opportunity, and to working with fellow members for a region free from the scourge of terrorism, separatism and extremism, which continue to threaten peace and stability in India's neighbourhood and beyond. PM Modi arrived in Uzbekistan Saturday for the first leg of his two-nation Central Asia tour that will also see him travelling to Bishkek for the Eurasian bloc heads of state summit early next week.PM Modi's remarks in his departure statement again underlined India's position that one of the original mandates of SCO, which includes Pakistan, was to fight the so-called three evils - terrorism, separatism and extremism.At the summit, PM Modi is also likely to reiterate that while India backs regional connectivity initiatives, these must align with the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all member states.Read more: PM Modi begins four-day Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan visit for SCO summit; what's on agenda PM Modi said, “I am confident that this visit will strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia, deepen our civilisational connect with the region, and advance our shared pursuit of peace, stability and prosperity, values that lie at the heart of India’s engagement with the world,” ahead of his departure for Tashkent.At the invitation of Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, PM Modi is on a two-day state visit to Tashkent.“In recent years, India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership has seen significant advancement. I look forward to my discussions with President Mirziyoyev on further deepening our cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, energy, and on advancing our shared visions of Viksit Bharat and Yangi Uzbekistan,” said Modi, who was welcomed by the Uzbek President at the airport.“I will also visit the Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies, a tribute to the close cultural and people-to-people ties that bind our two countries,” he added. Article Title: 'RSS vision is to see the world as one': Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat at New York event
Article Text:
'Unity in diversity in Bharat's DNA: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat

‘Be true to America’: RSS chief message to diaspora

Highlights responsibility towards others

Bhagwat offers interpretation of Dharma

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh ( RSS ) chief Mohan Bhagwat , addressing around 5,000 members of Indian-American organisations at Madison Square Garden in New York, spoke about unity, pluralism, individual responsibility and the obligations of the Indian diaspora, while arguing that material success alone cannot define a fulfilling life.Bhagwat was speaking at the “Universal Oneness Celebration”, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue. He framed his address around the idea of “oneness”, drawing parallels between the pluralism associated with the United States and what he described as Bharat’s “unity in diversity”.“When we say America, United States of America, one word is often discussed frequently. That is pluralism,” Bhagwat said. “And when we say Bharat, another word, another phrase is discussed: unity in diversity.”“For Bharat, this unity and diversity, both are in their DNA,” he said.Bhagwat said differences between people were a natural feature of life, but argued that these differences existed alongside an underlying sense of oneness.“So many styles of living. We appear different. We are different,” he said, pointing to differences in people's everyday needs and circumstances.“But there is innate oneness. That is why we feel for each other,” he added.He described diversity as the “decoration of oneness”, presenting unity not as the absence of differences but as something that exists beneath them.Bhagwat also linked this idea to what he described as the responsibilities of individuals, societies and nations. Nations, he said, should not be seen merely as geographical entities but as having a larger purpose.“These nations are not merely geographical entities. In the design of this universe, nations have to carry out a duty,” he said, quoting Swami Vivekananda's formulation that every nation has a message, a mission and a destiny.Turning to the Indian diaspora in the United States, Bhagwat said Indians living abroad had a primary responsibility towards the country where they lived and worked.“So we are Americans, and we should be true to America,” he said.He described this as a duty towards one's “karma bhumi” — the land where a person lives and works.“The diaspora, Indian diaspora, they have a duty to their karma bhumi. They must fulfill that. They should be loyal to their karma bhumi,” Bhagwat said.At the same time, he said Indians abroad could maintain a connection with Bharat as their “janma bhumi”, or birthplace, and could contribute to the country if they wished to do so after fulfilling their responsibilities to their adopted home.“But it is not obligatory,” he said.Instead, he said, the connection with Bharat should be reflected in the values carried by the diaspora.“Your janma bhumi expects you to live the values it has imparted on you,” Bhagwat said.Bhagwat also questioned the idea that professional success should be measured primarily through earnings and material possessions.“How much we earn is not important. How much we distribute is important,” he said.He asked whether a career could be reduced to money and material happiness, while acknowledging that material aspirations had a legitimate place in Hindu philosophy.“You think of career? Is career only money? Is career only material happiness?” Bhagwat asked.He referred to the four Purusharthas, saying that Artha and Kama represented important material dimensions of life alongside spiritual pursuits.“It is not denied. In four Purusharthas, Artha and Kama are two important Purusharthas related to material life,” he said.Bhagwat also referred to the traditional four stages of life — Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha and Sannyasa — arguing that people acquire different responsibilities as they move through life.“So you have to learn, you have to sustain life, and you have to give the advice, your experience to next generation,” he said.He argued that material abundance by itself could not guarantee fulfilment.“So the material happiness is transient, cannot satisfy,” Bhagwat said. “And if abundance of material happiness is there, it may fail also. And therefore there is no satisfaction.”Bhagwat's broader argument centred on the idea that human intelligence carried with it a responsibility towards others.Using the example of a hungry person watching someone eat, he said people instinctively recognise another person's suffering and cannot simply ignore it.“A simple experiment you can do, or I can challenge you to do. When you are taking your lunch or dinner, let a hungry man stand before you, and let him stare at your full platter with hungry eyes,” he said.“You can try; you will not do. Because we are human beings.”He contrasted human beings' ability to think and plan with the instinctive behaviour of animals, but said the ability to think also brought a responsibility to use that capacity correctly.“If you think in the right way, you go nearer to God. If you think in the wrong way, you go nearer to the animal kingdom,” he said.Bhagwat also offered a broader interpretation of “Dharma”, saying it should not be understood simply as religion or worship.“Dharma is not religion. It is not worship. It is beyond all this,” he said.He described Dharma as a sustaining principle that allows people and society to manage competing aspects of life and maintain balance.“It is the balance which sustains everything at once, simultaneously, and simultaneously everyone can progress,” Bhagwat said.He similarly argued that progress should not require either individuals or society to be suppressed.“Individual, society and environment, they have to proceed together, progress together,” he said, adding that different aspects of an individual's own life — body, mind and intellect — also had to advance together.Bhagwat concluded by returning to the idea of responsibility towards both one's place of work and birthplace.He called on people to fulfil their duties towards their “karma bhumi” as well as their “janma bhumi”, saying such an approach could help a world struggling with multiple challenges.“To that destiny and fulfill our duties in our karma bhumi as well as our janma bhumi,” he said.“If we do that, that will be a boon for the world struggling with all these problems and stumbling at every step.”
Article Summary: Rashtriya swayamsevak sangh ( rss ) chief mohan bhagwat spoke about unity, pluralism, individual responsibility and the obligations of the indian diaspora. He was speaking at the “universal oneness celebration”, organised by american hindus for engagement and dialogue.

Article Title: Pak drones, armed men spur searches in Poonch, Rajouri
Article Text:

JAMMU: Security forces have launched joint cordon-and-search operations along the LoC and after suspected Pakistan drones hovered in Poonch and Rajouri districts since Friday and reports emerged about movement of armed people in forested belts of Udhampur-Kathua and Rajouri, official sources said.One drone was spotted hovering over forward areas along the LoC in Poonch, prompting the searches early Saturday, the sources said. “The Pakistani drone was observed in Behrooti village in Mendhar sector late Friday evening. It moved towards Mangalnar-Dabrote, near the border, before returning to Pakistan,” a security source said.In Rajouri, Pakistani drones were spotted in a border area of Rumlidhara in Nowshera sector, leading to intensive searches. The operations are still continuing, aimed at ensuring that no weapons, narcotics or other contraband were air-dropped by the drones, the sources said.Separately, police, Army and paramilitary forces, have been combing vast forested patches in Udhampur, Kathua and Rajouri following information about suspicious movements of people, the sources said.The operations started late Friday evening in Khuban, Marta, Jopher, and adjoining areas of Udhampur-Kathua forests and were still underway. Two Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) terrorists were neutralised in these jungles in Feb this year. The duo had been holed up in a cave in Jopher area.In Rajouri, security forces have launched searches after locals in frontier villages such as Mogla and Narla reported movements of two armed people.

Article Title: Nepal floods: MEA says 88 Indians rescued, 287 still missing; forensic teams dispatched
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Saturday said that 88 Indian nationals have been rescued so far, while 287 remain missing amid the devastating floods in Nepal. It added that 128 persons of Indian origin are also reported missing. Moreover, the death toll from the floods has risen to 669.Four Indian nationals, Ripu Kumar, Chaneshwar Narzary, Kripa Shankar and Mohammed Minhajuddin, were rescued from a hydropower project in Rasuwa on Saturday and are expected to reach Kathmandu shortly.Six forensic expert teams from India are expected to reach Kathmandu to assist in analysing DNA samples for identification of mortal remains. The teams will support efforts to identify victims amid the large number of casualties following the floods.A specialised technical team from India, which reached Kathmandu on Friday for tunnel-rescue reconnaissance, began work in the affected area on Saturday.Based on its recommendations, a specialised tunnel rescue team with equipment is expected to reach Nepal on Saturday. The MEA also said 120 Indian nationals crossed into Nepal from China on Saturday.The Indian embassy issued emergency helpline numbers.Those seeking assistance can contact +977 985 131 6807 or +977 970 910 7500. A special control room which functions round-the-clock has been set up to assist those who are stranded.

Article Title: 'Strikes not just near LoC': Ex-Army chief Naravane details how India changed tactics in Op Sindoor
Article Text:
May 10, 2025: Screengrab from a video of Army and security personnel during Operation Sindoor (Photo: @adgpi on X via PTI)

Naravane dismisses Pak’s ability to take on India

On India-China border talks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Army chief General M M Naravane on Saturday described Operation Sindoor as "very necessary action", stating that it marked a significant shift in India's approach towards Pakistan. Naravane said India moved beyond targeting terrorist bases along the border to striking their supporters and infrastructure deep inside Pakistan, signalling a more assertive response to cross-border terrorism.Speaking to reporters in Vadodara after attending an event, Naravane, the 28th Chief of the Army Staff, said India’s earlier responses to terror attacks, including the Uri and Pulwama attacks, had largely focused on terrorist hideouts close to the border.“Operation Sindoor, which took place after the Pahalgam attack, was a very necessary action... Previously, whenever such attacks occurred, like after Uri, and Balakot strikes after Pulwama -- we were mostly targeting terrorist hideouts close to the border,” he said, news agency PTI reported.“But this time, the strikes carried out targeted their supporters and those who provide them backing, wherever they may be -- not just near the Line of Control, but deep inside Pakistan, in Muridke and Bahawalpur, from where they receive this support,” he added.Naravane said the operation sent a message that those supporting terrorism could not escape Indian action regardless of where they were located.“As our defence minister Rajnath Singh had said, 'we will enter their territory and eliminate them', and there will be no protection for them. So, this was a very significant shift in our modus operandi,” he said.Asked about reports of increased Pakistani activity in the Sir Creek sector and the reported “Operation Ababil”, Naravane said such activities take place but he did not have complete information about the reported operation.“These kinds of activities keep happening. I don't have complete information about this right now since I am retired,” he said.“I would like to say that whatever activity takes place, our forces always keep a close watch on it. There is nothing to panic about, and whatever action needs to be taken, appropriate action will be taken at the right time,” he added.Asked whether Pakistan was capable of taking on India, Naravane replied, “In my opinion, no.”On India-China relations, Naravane said the recent meeting between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi should be viewed against the backdrop of the long-standing boundary dispute between the two countries.“This discussion that took place, the 25th round of Special Representative-level talks between Ajit Doval from our side and Foreign Minister Wang Yi from China, is not happening for the first time,” he said.Naravane said the lack of a clearly demarcated boundary, both on maps and on the ground, was the key issue behind periodic disputes between the two countries.“Exactly where the boundary lies has not been clearly demarcated either on maps or on the ground. It is because of this lack of demarcation that occasional disputes arise between India and China,” he said.On theatre commands, Naravane said the debate over reorganising the armed forces along integrated theatre lines had been underway since the Kargil War.“The discussion on theaterisation first began after the Kargil War. It has already been 25 to 26 years since then. Theaterisation is not a new concept; it is a continuous process and an evolution,” he said.“Considering the way the nature of modern warfare is transforming and decision cycles are becoming progressively shorter, it is essential that we move toward theaterisation as expeditiously as possible,” the former Army chief added.Operation Sindoor was a significant demonstration of India's military and strategic capabilities, combining military and non-military measures to neutralise terrorist threats and deter Pakistani aggression. The multi-dimensional operation reinforced India’s zero-tolerance approach to terrorism while maintaining strategic restraint and securing international support.
Article Summary: Former army chief general m m naravane on saturday described operation sindoor as "very necessary action" he said india moved beyond targeting terrorist bases along the border to striking their supporters and infrastructure deep inside pakistan. “as our defence minister rajnath singh had said, 'we will enter their territory and eliminate them',” he said.

Article Title: 'Not interested right now': Rahul Gandhi on Sonia Gandhi memoir row, cites 'crime' against Kharge
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi on Sonia Gandhi memoir row

Also Read |

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday said he had “no interest” in the controversy surrounding the upcoming memoir of his mother and former Congress president Sonia Gandhi, saying his sole focus at present was the “crime” committed against party chief Mallikarjun Kharge.The Lok Sabha leader of opposition was responding to a reporter’s question at his press conference on the “purification” ritual conducted after Kharge’s rally in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, earlier this month."I call it a digression strategy. I have absolutely no interest in that right now. My interest lies in the crime that has been committed against Kharge ji," Rahul Gandhi said, demanding "justice" for the veteran politican.The controversy surrounding Sonia Gandhi’s biography, titled "Belonging: A Journey Of Love," arose from reports that publisher Penguin Random House India had declined to publish the book after she rejected proposed editorial changes.However, Penguin Random House India clarified in a statement on Friday that it was not the publisher of "Belonging" in India.“Any suggestion that Penguin Random House India decided not to publish ‘Belonging’ because the author declined editorial changes does not accurately reflect the circumstances,” the publisher said in a statement.However, it acknowledged that it remained “keen to publish the book”, while stressing that fact-checking and recommending editorial changes were part of its responsibility as a publisher.“As a publisher, it is both our prerogative and our responsibility to fact check and provide authors with recommendations that are in the best interests of their books. This is a normal part of the publishing process. Throughout the relevant discussions, Penguin Random House India’s position was that we remained willing and keen to publish the book.We will not comment further on confidential discussions with the author,” the statement added.On August 20, the birth anniversary of his father and former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi expressed his excitement over Sonia Gandhi’s biography.“I am happy, and so proud, that your story—‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’—will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story. Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia,” the Congress MP wrote on X.The book is scheduled to be published on November 10.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi on sonia gandhi memoir row: my interest lies in the crime that has been committed against kharge ji. The controversy surrounding sonia gandhi’s biography, titled "belonging: a journey of love," arose from reports that penguin random house india had declined to publish the book.

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat visited the Iskcon temple in New York during his ongoing US tour, where he participated in a food distribution initiative for homeless people and spoke about the role of Krishna consciousness in overcoming conflicts and divisions.Bhagwat visited the temple at 26 Second Avenue, where the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (Iskcon) began in 1966.Speaking to news agency ANI, Gauranga Das, a Governing Body Commissioner of Iskcon, said the organisation now has 1,300 temples across 120 countries.“In 1966, Swami Prabhupada officially founded the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (Iskcon). We are standing at 26 2nd Avenue, the same place from where Iskcon began, and today we have 1300 temples across 120 countries,” he said.Gauranga Das said Swami Prabhupada was credited with taking Hindu Sanatana Dharma to different parts of the world.Bhagwat penned a message during his visit, describing the venue as an inspiration and praising its contribution to spreading Krishna consciousness.“An inspiring venue which brought really a matchless gift of Sri Krishna consciousness to the world. I am humbled and surcharged with the feeling of pure sattvic love towards he who resides in everybody and everything.Heartiest thanks to all who arranged this inspiring event for me,” his message said.Gauranga Das said Bhagwat also spoke about how people could work together for global peace and harmony.In a post on X, he said Bhagwat offered a garland to Srila Prabhupada and inaugurated the distribution of the 100,000th meal under the Zero Hunger New York initiative at the Bhakti Center.Addressing devotees at the temple, Bhagwat spoke about the importance of consciousness in bringing people together despite conflicts and differences.“In today's world, there are so many conflicts, so many dualities. The only thing that unites is consciousness. That consciousness is Krishna Consciousness - we are one and we have been having it through these dualities of this world with the strong understanding that though there are so many diversities, dualities, conflicts, really it is all Krishna,” Bhagwat said.Anuttama Dasa, minister of communications and governing body commissioner of Iskcon, also welcomed Bhagwat's visit.“Mohan Bhagwat visited us and we are very grateful that he was here. A couple of weeks ago, Hema Malini was here. Both of them visited and we talked about how we can work together to try to promote God Consciousness and Krishna Consciousness values around the world,” he told ANI.He said Iskcon was seeking to promote an understanding of shared values at a time when the world was facing conflicts and polarisation.Bhagwat's visit to the Iskcon temple comes ahead of his scheduled address to the Indian diaspora at Madison Square Garden on Saturday at the ‘Universal Oneness Celebration’, being organised as part of the RSS centenary-year programmes.The event is being organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue and is expected to bring together Hindu-American organisations and members of the Indian diaspora around themes including shared heritage, interfaith dialogue and unity.The RSS chief arrived in New York on Tuesday as part of a three-nation outreach tour covering the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom.
Article Summary: Rss chief mohan bhagwat visited the iskcon temple in new york during his ongoing us tour. He participated in a food distribution initiative for homeless people and spoke about the role of krishna consciousness in overcoming conflicts and divisions. His visit comes ahead of his scheduled address to the indian diaspora at madison square garden on saturday.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan on Saturday for a two-day state visit, kicking off the first leg of his two-nation tour of Central Asia. He was received by Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the airport.Landmark buildings across the Uzbek capital, including the Hilton Hotel, were lit in the tricolour hues of the national flag.PM Modi lauded the artistry on X, saying, "The community welcome in Tashkent was a delightful celebration of India-Uzbekistan cultural ties! It included a performance by the Bollywood Battle Group on the evergreen 'Ude Jab Jab Zulfein Teri,' a fusion of Kathak and the energetic Andijan Polka, Kathak performance by students of the Lal Bahadur Shastri Centre for Indian Culture."The Prime Minister also laid a wreath at Yangi Uzbekistan Park, being accompanied by Uzbekistan President Mirziyoyev.PM Modi, who is visiting Uzbekistan for the fourth time, will hold delegation-level talks with Mirziyoyev in Tashkent to review and expand the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership.The discussions are expected to focus on trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, energy, education and people-to-people ties.The two leaders will also set the agenda for future bilateral engagement.The Prime Minister is also scheduled to visit the Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies. He said the visit would help deepen the “close cultural and people-to-people ties” between India and Uzbekistan.After his Uzbekistan visit, PM Modi will travel to Bishkek to attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit on August 31 and September 1, at the invitation of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov.The summit coincides with the SCO's 25th anniversary and will bring together leaders of its 10 member states — India, China, Russia, Iran, Belarus and other Central Asian countries.PM Modi is expected to meet Zhaparov and other SCO leaders during the summit. He will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games.India has been a full and active member of the SCO since 2017.“I look forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, anchored in Security, Connectivity and Opportunity, and to working with fellow members for a region free from the scourge of terrorism, separatism and extremism, which continue to threaten peace and stability in our neighbourhood and beyond,” PM Modi said.Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are among the leaders expected to attend the two-day SCO summit in Bishkek.The summit will bring together leaders of the 10-member grouping, which includes Russia, China, India, Pakistan, Iran, four Central Asian countries and Belarus.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif are also expected to participate in the plenary session.The SCO, which was founded with a focus on regional and economic cooperation, now has 15 dialogue partners and two observer countries, Afghanistan and Mongolia.PM Modi said he was confident that his visit would “strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia, deepen our civilisational connect with the region, and advance our shared pursuit of peace, stability and prosperity.”From Tashkent, the prime minister will travel to Bishkek to participate in the 26th SCO Summit, at the invitation of the President of the Kyrgyz Republic, Sadyr Zhaparov.

Russian president vladimir putin and chinese president xi jinping are among the leaders expected to attend the two-day summit. Article Title: Pakistani drone detected in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch, security forces put LoC sector on high alert
Article Text:

Drone tracked towards Mangalnar-Dabrote axis

Turkish military flights raise concerns

Security forces along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir have been put on high alert after fresh aerial activity originating from across the border was detected in the Poonch district.According to inputs from Army sources cited by news agency ANI, an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) from Pakistan was detected at around 8:05 pm on Friday.The drone was spotted hovering over the general area of Behrooti village in the Balakote area of Poonch's Mendhar sector, which falls under the operational area of responsibility of the 22 Jammu and Kashmir Rifles (22 JAK RIF).Military personnel tracked the UAV as it manoeuvred towards the Mangalnar-Dabrote side near the border before returning to Pakistan.Alert troops immediately logged the intrusion, following which the entire forward sector was placed under tight aerial and ground surveillance.Security forces launched the search operation at first light on Saturday in adjoining forward areas to check for any possible dropping of contraband or arms.Monitoring along the border remains active, and further official updates are awaited.The latest incident comes amid heightened security concerns along the India-Pakistan border and follows other suspected drone sightings reported in Jammu and Kashmir in recent weeks.Earlier this month, security forces launched a search operation after a suspected Pakistani drone was spotted over forward villages along the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir's Kathua district.The BSF and Jammu and Kashmir Police conducted searches to ensure that no weapons, explosives or other material had been dropped.A suspected Pakistani drone was also spotted in Rajouri's Sunderbani sector last month, after which security forces carried out a search operation but found nothing suspicious.Earlier in June, Army personnel opened fire after spotting a Pakistani drone over forward posts in the Balakote sector of Poonch, forcing it to retreat towards Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.Notably, the latest incident also comes days after an unusual increase in Turkish military transport flights to Pakistan raised concerns in Indian defence circles.Open-source flight trackers recorded a surge in Turkish C-130 Hercules and A400M aircraft flights between August 19 and 21, with the planes landing at Pakistani air bases, including Nur Khan, Masroor and Murid.There was speculation in defence circles that the flights may have carried military hardware, including unmanned aerial systems and air-defence equipment, although neither Pakistan nor Turkey officially confirmed the nature or cargo of the operations.Separately, security forces are carrying out massive search operations in the forested districts of Udhampur, Kathua and Rajouri following information about suspicious movement, according to news agency PTI.In Rajouri, another search operation was launched in Gaibas, Mithiyani, Mogla and Narla after villagers reported the movement of two suspected armed persons, believed to be terrorists.No contact with any suspected persons had been established so far, officials said.The latest incident in Poonch comes as security forces continue to maintain heightened surveillance along forward areas of Jammu and Kashmir.
Article Summary: Drone spotted hovering over behrooti village in balakote area of poonch's mendhar sector. Military personnel tracked the uav as it manoeuvred towards the mangalnar-dabrote side near the border before returning to pakistan. Comes amid heightened security concerns along the india-pakistan border.

Article Title: Have you done the truth test?
Article Text:
Thiruvalluvar captures the essence of this discipline in Kural 423:Epporul yaaryaarvaai ketpinum ApporulMeipporul kaanbadhu arivu.“Wisdom is to discover the truth in whatever is heard, irrespective of who says it.”Valluvar does not ask us to accept or reject an idea based on the identity of the speaker. He asks us to examine the truth within the statement.Iago’s words were believed because of who he appeared to be. Valluvar asks us to reverse that instinct: not “Who said this?” but “Is this true?”Truth is not measured by who speaks, but by what withstands examination.

Someone tells you that your closest friend has been speaking against you. At work, you hear that a colleague has spoiled your chances of a promotion. What do you do? Do you believe the person who told you, simply because you consider that person honest and dependable? Or do you pause and ask: How do I know if this is true?Shakespeare gave us a tragic answer to this question in ‘Othello’. Iago manipulates Othello by describing how his wife Desdemona’s handkerchief was with his friend Cassio, driving Othello into a jealous rage. The tragedy was not merely that Iago lied. It was that Othello failed to examine. He ended up killing Desdemona.How, then, does one ascertain truth? Is there a method by which we can distinguish what is real from what is merely reported, assumed or imagined?Interestingly, our ancestors believed in measuring everything accurately. Whether it was a piece of cloth or the jaggery needed for a pot of payasam, things had to be measured. In Tamil, there is a term, ‘Alavai iyal’ — the science of measurement. But measurement was not confined to physical objects. Indian philosophy also explored ways of measuring truth itself.These methods are called ‘pramanams’, means by which valid knowledge about what is true is obtained. Traditionally, six pramanams are described.The first is ‘pratyaksha’, or ‘kaatchi alavai’ — knowledge through direct perception using any of the senses. I smell gas and conclude there is a leak.The second is ‘anumana’, or ‘karuthal alavai’ — inference. I see smoke rising from a distance and infer that there must be a fire.The third is ‘agama pramanam’ or ‘urai alavai’ — knowledge obtained through texts.The fourth is ‘upamana pramanam’ or ‘uvamai alavai’ — knowledge through comparison. Understanding the unknown through knowledge about the known.The fifth is ‘arthapatti’ or ‘porul alavai’ — postulation from circumstances. The house is unusually quiet. We may infer that there was a big fight and now everybody is silent. It is not direct knowledge, but a conclusion drawn from circumstances.The sixth is ‘anupalabdhi’ or ‘inmai alavai’, knowledge through non-perception or absence. If someone claims to have seen a polar bear in Antarctica, the claim can be rejected because polar bears are native to the Arctic.These are not merely philosophical categories, but disciplines for the journey towards truth. Without them, our minds can easily become prisoners of assumptions and biases.Bias is perhaps our first obstacle. If someone we admire says something, we are inclined to accept it. If someone we dislike says the same thing, we may instinctively reject it. In both cases, we judge the statement by the person rather than examining its truth.The pramanas provide a framework to go beyond what our eyes can see without letting imagination outrun reason. They help us test assumptions, examine evidence and separate fact from illusion.
Article Summary: Thiruvalluvar captures the essence of this discipline in kural 423:epporul yaaryaarvaai ketpinum apporulmeipporul kaanbadhu arivu. Truth is not measured by who speaks, but by what withstands examination.

Article Title: Sonia memoir row deepens, Congress alleges government pressure
Article Text:
Controversy erupts as Penguin Random House India reportedly pulls out of Sonia Gandhi memoir deal, Congress calls it "murder of democracy."

NEW DELHI: A controversy has erupted over the Indian publication of Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging', with Penguin Random House India (PRHI) reportedly pulling out of the deal following differences with the former Congress president over certain suggested edits.Calling it a "murder of democracy", Congress functionary Ashok Gehlot alleged that "pressure was put on Penguin India to remove the portions related to Narendra Modi , RSS and China's occupation of Indian territory during Modi's rule".Penguin, for its part, issued a carefully worded statement saying: "PRHI is not the publisher of 'Belonging' in India. Any suggestion that PRHI decided not to publish it because the author declined editorial changes does not accurately reflect the circumstances." The publishing house, however, defended its "prerogative and responsibility" to fact-check manuscripts and make recommendations to authors. It also said it remained "willing and keen" to publish the book. Earlier this year, PRHI stopped the distribution of cartoonist Joe Sacco's 'The Once and Future Riot', on the Muzaffarnagar riots.Interestingly, the US publisher of the memoir, Alfred A Knopf, is also a division of Penguin Random House.The international launch of ‘Belonging: A Journey in Love’, featuring a photo of a young Sonia on its cover, is scheduled for Nov 10. There is a question mark over who the Indian rights of ‘Belonging’ belong to, but the buzz is that HarperCollins may bag them.Gehlot also questioned why PRHI wanted changes to the Indian edition if Knopf was ready to publish the book worldwide in its original form. “What is the reason or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?” he asked. “Why is this truth being hidden from the people of India? Will the Modi govt alter even the facts by pressuring publishers?” he added.Gehlot said the integrity and dignity with which Sonia had served the country were exemplary. “Suppressing the book of a person of such stature, a senior leader of the nation, and former leader of the opposition, is tantamount to the murder of freedom of expression,” he said.Deputy leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi said, “No doubt there are those in the BJP govt who have now become afraid of a book being read by the people of India.”Congress, from its official social media handle to frontal organisations such as Seva Dal, lashed out at what it called the BJP’s attempt to sabotage the book of a senior national figure.
Article Summary: Controversy erupts as penguin random house india reportedly pulls out of sonia gandhi memoir deal, congress calls it "murder of democracy" the publishing house defended its "prerogative and responsibility" to fact-check manuscripts and make recommendations to authors.

Article Title: India & China announce 8-point boundary consensus before Xi's visit, target early & substantial harvest in border delimitation
Article Text:
According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly.

NEW DELHI: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question - co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi this week - had led to an 8-point consensus, signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month.These included advancing consultations for an "early and substantial harvest" of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, expanding trans-border trade and rivers cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the SR talks.Building upon the outcomes from the last round of talks in 2024, the 2 sides agreed that the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management would advance discussions on an “Early and Substantial Harvest” of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference, said the joint statement.India and China had agreed last year to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC), to explore early harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas.The formulation was changed to early and substantial on this occasion.Two additional meeting points for military talks and 2 more channels of border military hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed upon to reinforce border management measures, according to both sides.“The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution,” said the MEA in a statement. Unlike the Chinese readout of the talks on Tuesday, the joint statement did not mention package settlement or solution, although the 2005 agreement talks about making adjustments to reach a package settlement.The two sides also reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the guidance received from Modi and Xi, maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas and creating an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations.According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. “The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management,” said the joint statement.Both sides also noted the progress on trans-border cooperation, with the Indian side appreciating the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra (KMY) in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.“Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view to work together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas,” said the joint statement.India and China also agreed to hold the next meeting of the India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of the relevant MoUs. It’s important for India that China shares hydrological information during emergency situations based on humanitarian considerations. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.
Article Summary: India and china announced wednesday that the special representatives (sr) dialogue on the boundary question had led to an 8-point consensus. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the sr talks. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of sr talks in india in 2027.

Article Title: 'Took off for Kathmandu blissfully unaware': Shashi Tharoor on deadly Nepal floods
Article Text:

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Thursday said that he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district when he left for Kathmandu on Wednesday."A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise," Tharoor said in a post on X.Tharoor added that the flooding had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges and washed away around 40 km of the Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi highway. Eight operational hydropower projects were also reported to have sustained heavy damage.Tharoor said he supported the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance to Nepal, adding that the country would need substantial help in responding to the destruction.He also expressed concern over the loss of life and those still missing, including Indians affected by the disaster."I fully support the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance.Nepal needs all the help it can get. My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon," Tharoor said.The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet, according to authorities.The scale of destruction has hampered rescue operations, with Nepalese officials reporting that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres (25 miles) of roads damaged.The Nepalese Army launched helicopter operations on Thursday morning, rescuing more than 100 people from flood-affected areas, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said. At least eight foreign nationals were also airlifted to Kathmandu, while army teams evacuated people trapped inside facilities associated with the Trishuli hydropower project.India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said five major groups, comprising around 288 Indian nationals, had been identified.“ The first group of 73 people who are working on the Trishuli-1 power project. Then, two separate groups of 37 and 49 nationals from Tamil Nadu, who traveled for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Samrat and Fly Everest Travels. There is a group of 32 Indian nationals from West Bengal who traveled with the help of Samrat Travels in Timure, which is in Rasuwa district.”“Then, a group of 61 Indian nationals from different states and then a group of 33 Indian nationals from Kerala. These are five major groups who comprise, by and large, 288 people that we are talking about,” he added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and offered India’s assistance for rescue and relief operations.“India is prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance,” PM Modi said, adding that Indian teams were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.The United Nations is also supporting the response, with agencies deploying personnel to assist local authorities. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warned of a “massive humanitarian need” as rescue and relief operations continued.The disaster has also renewed concerns over the Himalayan region’s exposure to extreme weather events and glacial hazards, particularly in areas where difficult terrain and damaged infrastructure can complicate emergency response.
Article Summary: Tharoor said he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in nepal on wednesday. The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in tibet.
